security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of malicious behavior, prompt injection, credential theft, or unauthorized command execution. The static findings are false positives from placeholder Cohere API keys, markdown code fences, and reference documentation links. Documentation should still prefer environment variable examples so users do not copy hardcoded secret patterns.

remediation.issue: API examples include direct api_key placeholder constructor calls.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variable examples and add a clear note not to hardcode production secrets.

content.value_statement: Unstructured text often needs reliable fields before it can feed apps or databases. This skill guides Python developers through Cohere v2 structured outputs and JSON Schema extraction.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to initialize and call Cohere ClientV2 in Python.
Demonstrates JSON Schema mode for validated structured responses.
Provides entity extraction schemas for people, organizations, locations, dates, and documents.
Explains classification outputs with enums for stable downstream logic.
Covers schema reuse, nested objects, formats, and validation patterns.
Includes guidance for batching, parsing, error handling, and token monitoring.
limitations: Requires a Cohere account, API access, and the Python SDK.
Does not execute requests or validate live API behavior by itself.
Some JSON Schema features are unsupported by Cohere structured outputs.
Examples may need adaptation for privacy, compliance, and production security.

use_cases.title: Data Engineering Pipelines
use_cases.description: Extract normalized fields from documents before loading validated records into databases or analytics systems.

use_cases.title: Product Feedback Classification
use_cases.description: Classify user comments into sentiment and aspect categories with controlled labels.

use_cases.title: Research Document Review
use_cases.description: Identify people, organizations, events, and dates across articles or reports.

prompt_templates.title: Extract One Entity Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner entity extraction from one text sample.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cohere-v2-python skill to design a Python example that extracts people, organizations, locations, and dates from this text: [paste text].

prompt_templates.title: Create an Invoice Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate schema design for business documents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, create a JSON Schema mode plan for extracting invoice vendor details, dates, line items, tax, and totals.

prompt_templates.title: Build Batch Extraction Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pipeline design for repeated document processing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a batch extraction workflow with schema reuse, parsing, retries, token monitoring, and storage preparation.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Cohere v2 extraction design for schema gaps, privacy risks, error handling, rate limits, and downstream validation needs.

output_examples.input: Extract entities from a conference announcement.
output: Entities are grouped by person, organization, location, event, and date.
Required fields are identified before optional enrichment fields.
The result is ready for a schema-backed parser.

output_examples.input: Design a sentiment classifier for support tickets.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a controlled category set, schema requirements, and retry guidance for invalid responses.

output_examples.input: Review an extraction pipeline for production use.
output_examples.output: The response highlights API key handling, rate limits, parsing safeguards, token monitoring, and application-level validation.

best_practices: Keep API keys in environment variables and never store production secrets in examples or repositories.
Start with required fields, then add optional fields after testing real documents.
Use enums for categories that must feed databases, dashboards, or routing rules.
anti_patterns: Do not paste sensitive medical, legal, or personal data without an approved privacy process.
Do not rely on free-form JSON mode when downstream systems require strict fields.
Do not skip error handling for parsing, rate limits, or incomplete model responses.

faq.question: Does this skill call Cohere directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for building Python code that uses Cohere.

faq.question: Can it extract entities from documents?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains schemas and prompts for extracting structured entities from text.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Live use requires a Cohere API key. Store it in an environment variable.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content can guide those tools when they help write or review Python integrations.

faq.question: Does JSON Schema mode guarantee every business rule?
faq.answer: No. It enforces supported schema structure, but application validation is still needed.

faq.question: Is it production ready by itself?
faq.answer: No. Add logging, retries, rate limiting, privacy controls, and tests for your data.
